1988A&A...200..312W.title: The Multi-Resolution Clean and its application to the short-spacing problem in interferometry

flux_recovery_details.evidence: At peak-to-noise 20, the 5′ circular model has true flux 1002; MRC recovers 962 with a flat cumulative profile, while CLEAN recovers 563 with a strongly changing profile.

flux_recovery_details.scope: Realistic clean-map model reused as truth (≈30′ / 90 beams)

execution_context.aperture_region: Full model extent in dirty-map experiment

flux_recovery_details.evidence: From a true flux of 10,000 arbitrary units, MRC recovers 9358 (93.6%); CLEAN recovers 6910 (69.1%) and leaves the negative bowl present.

flux_recovery_details.scope: MRC vs conventional CLEAN recovered integrated flux (Table 1)
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Across Table 1 models MRC recovers substantially more integrated flux than CLEAN (e.g. 962 vs 563 of 1002 at 5′; 2788 vs 653 of 4010 at 10′). At low SNR MRC can over-recover.

2008ISTSP...2..793C.title: Multiscale CLEAN Deconvolution of Radio Synthesis Images

flux_recovery_details.scope: M31 VLA C-config simulation (Table II total recovered flux)

execution_context.frequency: X-band context in related sweeps; M31 table is continuum sim

flux_recovery_details.evidence: Table II: Multiscale CLEAN recovers 1,495 Jy (exact match to the table reference), vs Högbom 1,474 Jy, Clark 1,326 Jy, MRC 1,546 Jy, MEM 1,486 Jy.
Source-size and noise sweeps report recovered-flux fraction vs maximum scale and SNR; Multiscale CLEAN retains accurate flux estimates down to SNR ~4, while MEM overestimates from SNR as high as 100.

flux_recovery_details.scope: Real VLA D-config H I channel of NGC 1058

execution_context.aperture_region: Source region (multiscale flux stable when enlarged)

flux_recovery_details.evidence: On real NGC 1058 H I data, Multiscale CLEAN recovered 3.08 Jy integrated flux vs 0.32 Jy for Högbom CLEAN; Högbom flux was strongly region-dependent due to the negative bowl.

2011A&A...532A..71R.title: A multi-scale multi-frequency deconvolution algorithm for synthesis imaging in radio interferometry

flux_recovery_details.scope: Noise-free EVLA Taylor-order test, 2:1 band, four Taylor terms (Figure 4)
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Noise-free Taylor-order test: for a 2:1 band and four Taylor terms, reference-frequency peak-flux error is about 1 part in 1,000 (with DR ~100,000 and spectral-index error ~0.01).

2014MNRAS.444..606O.title: WSClean: an implementation of a fast, generic wide-field imager for radio astronomy

flux_recovery_details.scope: 100×1 Jy MWA simulation, zenith, 12 w-layers (vs CASA 1.34%)

execution_context.aperture_region: AEGEAN catalogue on 100 simulated 1 Jy sources

flux_recovery_details.evidence: At zenith with 12 w-layers, WSClean reports 1.31% AEGEAN source-flux standard error (and 0.94 mJy/beam residual RMS) versus CASA 1.34% and 1.90 mJy/beam.

flux_recovery_details.scope: MWA simulation grid (zenith and 10° zenith angle)
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Across controlled tests the paper summarizes WSClean as having 2–33% lower source-flux errors (and 0–49% lower residual RMS) than CASA.

flux_recovery_details.scope: LOFAR LBA semi-realistic simulation vs beam radius (Figure 9)

execution_context.aperture_region: Point sources vs distance from beam centre / HPBW

flux_recovery_details.evidence: Simulation measures (estimated S₅₀ − true S₅₀)/true S₅₀ versus beam-radius distance. Direction-independent narrowband imaging shows strong negative radial bias; DD HMP-WB and SSD-WB cluster much closer to zero (SSD visually tighter).

2022A&A...664A.134S.title: Deep learning-based imaging in radio interferometry

flux_recovery_details.scope: 10,000 synthetic radio-galaxy tests, noiseless radionets model
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Core specific-intensity mean relative deviations: noiseless network −4.354% ± 6.662%; image-noise-trained 0.613% ± 12.402%; WSClean −13.645% ± 24.312%.

flux_recovery_details.scope: Radionets vs fixed WSClean config on synthetic cores
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Network core-intensity bias/scatter is smaller than the reported WSClean mean deviation (−13.6% ± 24.3%), though large dispersions show near-zero mean bias ≠ accurate per-source flux.

2022ApJ...939L...4D.title: First AI for Deep Super-resolution Wide-field Imaging in Radio Astronomy: Unveiling Structure in ESO 137-006

flux_recovery_details.scope: ESO 137-006 AGN photometry, MeerKAT continuum bands

execution_context.aperture_region: AGN region (CLEAN within dirty-beam main lobe; ML over active pixels)

flux_recovery_details.evidence: At 1053 MHz, uSARA, AIRI, and CLEAN recover 143, 143, and 146 mJy; at 1399 MHz 124, 125, and 123 mJy. Agreement is a real-data consistency check, not truth error.

2023MNRAS.522.5558W.title: Scalable precision wide-field imaging in radio interferometry: I. uSARA validated on ASKAP data

flux_recovery_details.scope: ASKAP fields: Abell 3395, PKS 2014-55, SPT2023, PKS 2130-538

execution_context.aperture_region: Manually drawn regions (~2σ WSClean contour; shared per source/sub-band)

flux_recovery_details.evidence: Tabulated integrated diffuse fluxes across sub-bands for multiple sources (e.g. Abell 3395 phoenix Table 3; PKS 2014-55 Table 4; SPT2023 relic Table 5). Closest agreement on PKS 2130-538: 117.2 mJy uSARA vs 115.5 mJy WSClean restored/smoothed at 943 MHz.

2023MNRAS.522.5576W.title: Scalable precision wide-field imaging in radio interferometry: II. AIRI validated on ASKAP data

flux_recovery_details.scope: ASKAP AIRI vs uSARA / WSClean integrated fluxes (Tables 1–4)

execution_context.aperture_region: Hand-drawn regions adjusted to AIRI morphology

flux_recovery_details.evidence: AIRI integrated fluxes tabulated per field/sub-band (e.g. Abell phoenix Table 1; PKS 2014-55 Table 2; SPT2023 relic Table 3). PKS 2130-538 full-band AIRI 116.7 mJy agrees closely with companion uSARA/WSClean; apertures differ from the uSARA paper.

2026arXiv260309162W.title: POLISH'ing the Sky: Wide-Field and High-Dynamic Range Interferometric Image Reconstruction with Application to Strong Lens Discovery

flux_recovery_details.scope: SEP flux RMSE on true-positive detections (Table 3)
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Table 3 flux RMSE: CLEAN 3.2625×10⁻⁴ Jy/px (best), POLISH 1.9504×10⁻³, POLISH+ 3.8411×10⁻³, POLISH++ 3.1703×10⁻³ — CLEAN superior for flux fidelity.

flux_recovery_details.scope: CLEAN vs POLISH / POLISH+ / POLISH++ flux RMSE
flux_recovery_details.evidence: Learned POLISH variants have higher flux RMSE than CLEAN; attributed to nonlinear learned reconstruction lacking explicit flux calibration.
